subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Maslow's hierarchy of needs is usually shown as having how many levels?
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explain: Maslow's hierarchy has five levels: physiological, safety, social, esteem and self-actualisation needs.

questions.q: Which theorist is associated with scientific management and paying workers by piece rate?
options: F.W. Taylor
Abraham Maslow
Frederick Herzberg
Elton Mayo
questions.explain: Taylor's scientific management proposed that workers are mainly motivated by money and should be paid according to output (piece rate).

questions.q: According to Herzberg's two-factor theory, which of the following is a motivator rather than a hygiene factor?
options: Recognition for achievement
Rate of pay
Working conditions
Company policy
questions.explain: Herzberg classed recognition and achievement as motivators, while pay, conditions and policy are hygiene factors that only prevent dissatisfaction.

questions.q: Job enrichment involves which of the following?
options: Giving employees more challenging tasks and greater responsibility
Giving employees more tasks of a similar level of difficulty
Moving employees between different jobs of the same level
Paying employees more money for each unit produced
questions.explain: Job enrichment adds more demanding tasks and responsibility, unlike job enlargement or job rotation which keep the level of work the same.

questions.q: A factory worker who repeats the same task all day has become bored and demotivated. Which non-financial method would best address this by switching them between different tasks?
options: Job rotation
Piece rate
Commission
Redundancy
questions.explain: Job rotation moves workers between different tasks, reducing boredom from repetitive work.

questions.q: The span of control refers to which of the following?
options: The number of subordinates directly under the control of a manager
The number of levels in the organisation's hierarchy
The route through which instructions are passed down
The process of passing authority to a subordinate
questions.explain: The span of control is the number of employees a manager is directly responsible for.

questions.q: In an organisation chart, the chain of command is best described as which of the following?
options: The line of authority through which instructions pass from top to bottom
The number of people one manager controls
The removal of layers of management
The informal social links between workers
questions.explain: The chain of command is the path of authority down which orders and instructions are passed in an organisation.

questions.q: Delegation in a business means which of the following?
options: Passing authority down to a subordinate to carry out a task
Removing a layer of management from the hierarchy
Increasing the number of levels in the hierarchy
Making all decisions without consulting anyone
questions.explain: Delegation is giving a subordinate the authority to carry out a task, though overall responsibility stays with the manager.

questions.q: An autocratic leadership style is one in which which of the following happens?
options: The leader makes decisions without consulting employees
Employees are fully involved in making decisions
The leader lets employees make their own decisions
Decisions are always made by majority vote
questions.explain: Autocratic leaders make decisions alone and simply tell employees what to do, unlike democratic or laissez-faire styles.

questions.q: A business removes several middle-management layers, so each remaining manager now supervises more workers directly. What is the most likely result?
options: A flatter structure with a wider span of control
A taller structure with a narrower span of control
A longer chain of command
The end of all delegation in the business
questions.explain: Delayering removes management levels, creating a flatter hierarchy and widening each manager's span of control.

questions.q: A person specification sets out which of the following?
options: The qualifications, skills and qualities required of the ideal candidate
The tasks and duties involved in the job
The wage and working hours for the role
The history and aims of the business
questions.explain: A person specification describes the ideal candidate, while the job description lists the tasks and duties of the job.

questions.q: Induction training is training given to which employees?
options: New employees when they first start a job
Only senior managers
Employees who are about to be made redundant
Only workers sent to an external college
questions.explain: Induction training introduces new employees to the business, their role, colleagues and procedures when they begin work.

questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of internal recruitment compared with external recruitment?
options: The candidate is already known to the business and needs less induction
It brings completely new ideas into the business from outside
It always gives a wider choice of applicants
It avoids creating a vacancy anywhere in the business
questions.explain: Internal candidates are already familiar with the business, so recruitment is quicker and cheaper and less induction is needed.

questions.q: On-the-job training is best described as which of the following?
options: Training carried out while doing the job at the workplace
Training given away from the workplace at a college
Training given only to senior managers
Training given just before a worker is dismissed
questions.explain: On-the-job training takes place at the workplace while the employee actually does the job, often by watching an experienced worker.

questions.q: A supermarket must fill a senior manager post and wants someone who already understands its systems and culture. Which recruitment method is most suitable?
options: Internal recruitment
External recruitment through a newspaper advert
External recruitment through an employment agency
Making an existing worker redundant
questions.explain: Internal recruitment promotes an existing employee who already knows the supermarket's systems and culture.

questions.q: Which of the following are the essential parts of the communication process?
options: A sender, a message, a receiver and feedback
Only a sender and a message
Only written documents
Only face-to-face conversation
questions.explain: Effective communication requires a sender, a message sent through a medium, a receiver and feedback confirming understanding.

questions.q: Two-way communication is communication in which which of the following occurs?
options: The receiver can respond and give feedback to the sender
Information flows in one direction only
No medium is used at all
Only managers are allowed to speak
questions.explain: Two-way communication allows the receiver to reply and give feedback, unlike one-way communication.

questions.q: Which of the following is a barrier to effective communication?
options: Using technical jargon the receiver does not understand
Giving clear feedback to the sender
Choosing an appropriate medium for the message
Keeping the message short and clear
questions.explain: Jargon the receiver cannot understand distorts the meaning and prevents the message being received correctly.

questions.q: Which method is most appropriate for sending long, detailed instructions that need to be kept as a permanent record for many employees?
options: A written report or email
An informal chat in the corridor
A quick verbal phone call
Word of mouth through the grapevine
questions.explain: Written communication suits long, detailed messages because it provides an accurate, permanent record that can be re-read.

questions.q: A manager finds that verbal messages passed through several people reach workers in a distorted form. Which improvement would best reduce this problem?
options: Send a written message directly to all the workers
Add more people to the chain of communication
Rely more on informal gossip
Stop asking workers for feedback
questions.explain: Sending a written message directly to workers removes the intermediaries that distort a verbal message passed along a chain.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies (0450) syllabus; People in Business
